reuse.why: Extends the shared getScheduledAmount and computes the tolerance with the existing getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules, the same helper the matching code uses.

duplication.why: No logic is duplicated; every caller passes its op to the one helper.

placement.why: The worst-case rule stays in shared/schedules getScheduledAmount next to the ranged rule, and callers in both packages only pass their own op.

scope.why: Touches every getScheduledAmount caller, which is what the rule needs, though it also changes display and edit-reducer callers (SchedulesTable amount cell, useScheduleEdit op switching) where planning semantics are debatable.

maintainability.why: One definition with an explicit op argument is easy to own; inserting amountOp before the inverse boolean reorders a positional signature, a minor wart.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All callers route through getScheduledAmount, which uses getApproxNumberThreshold

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount, called with the op by every caller in loot-core and desktop-client
